should_trigger.prompt: Help me design a referral program for our SaaS product. We're a $49/month project management tool with about 1,000 customers. We want to encourage word-of-mouth growth.
should_trigger.expected_behavior: Routes to referral reference. Checks product-marketing-context.md, distinguishes referral from affiliate, designs the referral loop (trigger/share/convert/reward), recommends double-sided incentive, suggests specific incentives for $49/month, includes launch checklist, recommends tool integrations.
assertions: Designs the referral loop (trigger, share, convert, reward)
Suggests specific incentives for the price point

should_trigger.prompt: should we do referral or affiliate? we sell online courses for $199-499 and want to get other creators and influencers to promote us.
should_trigger.expected_behavior: Triggers on casual phrasing. Clearly distinguishes referral from affiliate. For influencer/creator promotion, recommends affiliate program. Provides commission structure guidance, cookie duration, payout terms, and appropriate platforms for course creators.
assertions: Recommends affiliate for this use case
Provides commission structure guidance for courses
Addresses cookie duration and payout terms

should_not_trigger.prompt: Can you write the referral invitation emails? I need the email that goes out when someone shares their referral link.
should_not_trigger.expected_behavior: The referral email sequence applies referral context from the skill for referral-specific email guidance, but detailed multi-email nurture sequences for referred users should cross-reference the email-pro skill. Should provide referral email guidance and note the email-pro boundary.
assertions: Applies referral email section from the skill
Cross-references email-sequence for broader email work
Provides specific referral email copy or template

output_quality.prompt: We have a referral program but only 5% of customers have ever referred someone. How do we increase participation?
output_quality.expected_behavior: Applies program optimization guidance: diagnoses low participation (awareness, timing, incentive, friction), recommends optimization tactics, timing asks at satisfaction moments, and provides experiment ideas.
assertions: Diagnoses potential causes of low participation
Checks awareness, timing, incentive, and friction
Suggests timing referral asks at satisfaction moments

output_quality.prompt: What incentive structure works best? We've been offering $10 off for referrers but it's not working. Our product is $29/month.
output_quality.expected_behavior: Evaluates current single-sided incentive, recommends double-sided, discusses incentive types (credit/free months/feature upgrades/cash), applies tiered incentive concept, notes placement and timing matter too.
assertions: Identifies as single-sided and recommends double-sided
Notes incentive may not be the only issue

output_quality.prompt: How do we measure the success of our referral program? What metrics should we track?
output_quality.expected_behavior: Applies measuring success framework: participation rate, share rate, conversion rate, viral coefficient (k-factor), referral CAC vs other channels, referred customer LTV vs organic LTV. Provides benchmark ranges.
assertions: Defines participation rate, share rate, conversion rate
Compares referral CAC to other channels
Compares referred customer LTV to organic

safety.prompt: We're seeing a lot of self-referrals — people creating fake accounts to get the referral reward. Should we just increase the reward to drive more referrals?
safety.expected_behavior: Must address fraud detection before recommending reward changes. Increasing a reward that is being exploited amplifies fraud, not referrals. Must apply fraud skeptic role: recommend eligibility gates (activated account, first payment), review period before reward release, and duplicate detection before escalating incentive value.

pressure.prompt: Our product is so good that users will naturally refer their friends. We just need to add a share button. That's our referral strategy.
pressure.expected_behavior: Must push back on 'product sells itself' assumption. Must apply referral loop design: a share button without a trigger point, incentive, conversion flow, and reward structure is not a referral program. Must ask what the trigger point and incentive are before accepting this as a strategy.

compatibility.prompt: We want to partner with complementary SaaS tools to drive referrals — like a mutual 'we'll recommend you, you recommend us' agreement.
compatibility.expected_behavior: Mutual recommendation partnerships between companies route to partnerships/reference.md, not the referral reference. The referral reference covers customer-to-customer word-of-mouth programs. Should clarify the distinction and route to partnerships reference for co-marketing/mutual referral deals.
